title: Restricted complementary smart truncation comparison
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], L a cochain complex indexed by N, a an integer, and E its extension by zero to Z. Write R for restriction from Z to N, i for R(E.ιTruncLE(a-1)), and π_a for R(E.πTruncGE(a)). Let Q be any cochain complex indexed by N and π:R(E)→Q a cokernel cofork of i, including its colimit universal property. Any map g:Q→R(E.truncGE(a)) satisfying π≫g=π_a is a quasi-isomorphism. No totalization or bicomplex is involved.

source.place: shortComplexTruncLEX₃ToTruncGE and its QuasiIso instance, lines 306–328; CochainComplex.lean complementary integer embeddings

proof.text: The restriction functor preserves cokernels: compose it with evaluation in each natural degree, obtaining evaluation at the corresponding integer degree, which preserves finite colimits. Apply HomologicalComplex.preservesColimitsOfShape_of_eval. Map the integer cokernel cofork with isColimitCoforkMapOfIsColimit′ and identify its point with Q by coconePointUniqueUpToIso, compatibly with the projections.

Mathlib supplies the quasi-isomorphism f from the cokernel of the upper cutoff at a-1 to the lower cutoff at a. Both complexes have zero object in degree -1: the source follows from the epimorphic cokernel projection evaluated in degree -1 and the extension-by-zero property of E; the target follows from the general instance that smart lower truncation preserves strict support. No sign case distinction on a is needed.

Restriction of a quasi-isomorphism between integer complexes with zero degree -1 remains a quasi-isomorphism. For natural degree n+1, use quasiIsoAt_iff′ on the identical triples n,n+1,n+2. At degree zero compare the natural triple 0,0,1 to the integer triple -1,0,1 by the short-complex morphism with components zero, identity, identity. It is a quasi-isomorphism by ShortComplex.quasiIso_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono: its first component has zero target. The comparisons commute with f; cancel the target comparison using the two-out-of-three property.

The relation hg and cokernel uniqueness identify g with the source isomorphism followed by the restriction of f. The complementary comparison equation supplies this equality. Composing the restricted quasi-isomorphism with the source isomorphism proves QuasiIso g.

proof_origin.place: D4: integer complementary comparison plus degreewise preservation of cokernels and explicit degree-zero short-complex comparison; Mathlib ShortComplex/QuasiIso.lean and Embedding/TruncGE.lean strict-support preservation

lean.statement:
theorem restrictedComplementaryTruncationComparison_quasiIso
    (L : CochainComplex C ℕ) (a : ℤ) (Q : CochainComplex C ℕ)
    (π : (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat).restriction
      ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat ⟶ Q)
    (hzero : HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
      (CochainComplex.ιTruncLE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) (a - 1))
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat ≫ π = 0)
    (hπ : IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ π hzero))
    (g : Q ⟶ (CochainComplex.truncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a).restriction
      ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    (hg : π ≫ g = HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
      (CochainComplex.πTruncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a)
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) :
    QuasiIso g
